pills.text: 17. CONSTITUTIONAL DICTATORSHIP AS A DESIGN PROBLEM - OPTIONAL
A CONSTITUTION NEEDS CRISIS CAPACITY, BUT UNCHECKED CRISIS POWER
[ANALYSIS] THE MODERN ANSWER SHOULD JUDGE THE PROVISIONS TOGETHER
EMERGENCY POWER CONCENTRATES AUTHORITY TEMPORARILY UNDER LEGAL FORMS.

groups.heading: OPTIONAL DOCTRINE / CASE
items: 16. Safety-valve versus constitutional dictatorship - optional
17. Constitutional dictatorship as a design problem - optional
[ANALYSIS] Both sides are partly correct: a Constitution needs crisis capacity, but unchecked crisis power can destroy the
order it claims to preserve.

groups.heading: ADVANCED LIMIT
items: [ANALYSIS] The modern answer should judge the provisions together with 44th Amendment safeguards, judicial review and political federalism.
Emergency power concentrates authority temporarily under legal forms.
The risk is normalisation: crisis standards may become ordinary governance.
Procedural safeguards, sunset/renewal, reasons, parliamentary opposition, judicial access and protected rights prevent normalisation.

groups.heading: COMPARATIVE NUANCE
items: India's strongest design choice is not merely special-majority approval but non-suspendable Articles 20 and 21.
The remaining weakness is information asymmetry: Parliament and courts depend on executive material concerning threat and State breakdown.
